# Jimmy Essex

Jimmy Essex is a British actor and writer known for his work across television, stage, and streaming platforms . His career encompasses a range of roles that highlight his versatility, from a long-running part in the Channel 4 soap opera *Hollyoaks* to a critically noted West End theatre debut in the play *GHBoy* , . He has also appeared in high-profile productions such as Netflix's fantasy series *The Sandman*, demonstrating his ability to navigate different facets of the entertainment industry . Beyond performance, Essex has contributed as a writer to live storytelling events, further establishing his creative presence . A significant aspect of his public profile includes his vocal advocacy for the arts sector, particularly concerning government support during the COVID-19 pandemic . On a personal level, he is married to his partner, Charles, whom he refers to as his "husband and best friend," and their relationship has been a subject of public interest , . His journey reflects a progression from early-stage talent shows and live tours to established roles in both mainstream and niche entertainment, positioning him as a multifaceted figure within contemporary British arts.

## Early Life and Education

Information regarding Jimmy Essex's early life, including his precise date of birth and place of birth, is not available in the provided sources. However, the materials do indicate that his passion for performance began at a young age and was formally cultivated through specialized education. He trained at The Urdang Academy in London, a prestigious institution known for its focus on musical theatre and performance arts, which equipped him with foundational skills for his future career . This educational background is a crucial element in understanding his professional trajectory, as it represents the formal initiation into his chosen field before he embarked on his public career in entertainment. Prior to gaining widespread recognition as an actor, Essex accumulated practical performance experience through appearances on popular talent and reality television shows. He performed professionally on both *The X Factor* and *Britain's Got Talent*, participating in one of the UK's most visible platforms for aspiring performers . These appearances likely provided him with valuable exposure and experience in live performance under pressure. Furthermore, his career included touring with established UK artists, including the pop group The Saturdays . This period of his life, spent on tour, would have honed his skills in live audience engagement and collaborative performance, serving as a formative step before he transitioned more fully into acting roles on screen and stage. His early career path demonstrates a blend of formal training and diverse real-world performance opportunities, laying the groundwork for his later successes in more structured theatrical and television environments.

## Career Overview

Jimmy Essex's professional career spans multiple domains within the performing arts, showcasing a versatile artist who has successfully navigated television, stage, and writing. His work is characterized by a commitment to diverse and often complex characters, ranging from the dramatic soap opera world of *Hollyoaks* to the intimate and challenging setting of a West End production , . He identifies theatre as his original artistic passion, a sentiment that underscores his dedication to his craft and informs his approach to performance . This deep-rooted connection to the stage is evident in his choice of roles and his public statements about the importance of live performance. In addition to his primary identity as an actor, Essex has also demonstrated a creative capacity beyond performance by contributing as a writer. His involvement in writing for 'Picture This', a live ekphrastic storytelling event, highlights his broader engagement with the arts and his desire to be involved in the creative process at multiple levels . This dual role as both performer and creator adds a layer of depth to his profile, distinguishing him from many actors who primarily focus on performance alone. His career path reflects a deliberate progression from initial exposure on talent shows to a sustained presence in television, followed by a significant milestone with a West End debut, illustrating a well-rounded and evolving professional journey in the competitive entertainment industry , .

## Television Work

Jimmy Essex achieved significant prominence through his television career, particularly for his portrayal of Adam Donovan in the long-running Channel 4 soap opera *Hollyoaks* , , . This role served as a major platform for his work, allowing him to reach a wide audience over a two-year period . The character of Adam Donovan was central to several storylines, and the dramatic exit of his character became a memorable plot twist within the series. According to the provided information, Adam Donovan was killed off by his father, Glenn Donovan, played by Bob Cryer, in a storyline involving betrayal and patricide . This method of departure is a notable and impactful moment in the show's history, suggesting that Essex's performance was integral to the emotional weight of the narrative. His tenure on the show concluded in May of the prior year relative to the context's timeline, marking the end of a substantial chapter in his television career . Following his time on *Hollyoaks*, Essex expanded his portfolio with a guest appearance in the acclaimed Netflix fantasy series *The Sandman* . This project represents a move into the realm of high-budget, internationally distributed streaming content, broadening his appeal beyond traditional television viewership and placing him alongside a new generation of performers in the fantasy genre. While the specific character he portrayed in *The Sandman* is not detailed in the sources, his participation in the production signifies a significant achievement and a testament to his growing reputation as a capable actor in diverse genres. His television credits demonstrate a clear evolution, moving from the serialized drama of a soap opera to the global scale of a streaming blockbuster, highlighting his adaptability and range as a performer.

## Stage Performances

A defining aspect of Jimmy Essex's career is his deep-seated passion for theatre, which he considers his original artistic calling , . This commitment culminated in his professional West End stage debut in December 2020. He took on the lead role of Robert Finch in the play *GHBoy*, a production centered on the sensitive and complex themes of chemsex addiction, infidelity, self-discovery, and trauma recovery , . The play, written by Paul Harvard, resonated deeply with Essex, who found the material personally meaningful due to its exploration of identity, stigma, and misconceptions surrounding gay culture . His performance at the Charing Cross Theatre marked a significant milestone, transitioning him from screen-based work to the demanding environment of live theatre , . The production ran from December 3, 2020, to December 20, 2020, indicating a short but intense run in the heart of London's theatre district . This debut was not merely a career step but a fulfillment of a lifelong vocation for Essex, as he articulated in interviews, framing the role as a profound artistic statement . Beyond this major role, his involvement in the arts extends to choreography and teaching. As of 2018, he co-founded Beyond Performing Arts, an innovative school dedicated to the performing arts, where he serves as an Acting & Dance Teacher and Choreographer . This role demonstrates his contribution to nurturing the next generation of performers and his expertise in both acting and movement, solidifying his reputation as a comprehensive artist with a strong foundation in classical and contemporary performance disciplines.

## Other Notable Projects

Beyond his primary work in television and theatre, Jimmy Essex has engaged in other creative projects that showcase his multifaceted talents. One of the most significant of these is his contribution as a writer. He was listed among the writers for 'Picture This', a live ekphrastic storytelling event produced by Ye You Productions . The event took place at the Marylebone Theatre on November 15, 2023, and involved telling stories inspired by visual art . This involvement indicates that his creative output is not limited to performing; he actively participates in the development of narrative content, adding another dimension to his professional identity. In the realm of advertising, Essex has also had a commercial presence. He was featured as the face of the Euro Cup Coca-Cola advert, which would have placed his image before a massive audience during a major international sporting event . This type of endorsement suggests that he is recognized not only for his acting abilities but also for his marketability and public persona. His body of work thus extends beyond scripted roles into the realms of live storytelling, brand representation, and behind-the-scenes creative collaboration. This breadth of experience underscores his versatility and his active engagement with various forms of artistic expression, from the intimate confines of a theatre stage to the global reach of a major sports broadcast campaign. These varied projects paint a picture of an artist who is not confined to a single medium but thrives across a spectrum of performance and creative fields.

## Personal Life

In his personal life, Jimmy Essex is in a committed relationship with Charles, who he publicly refers to as his "husband and best friend" . Their relationship has been a subject of public interest, particularly following a significant milestone that Essex shared with his followers on social media. After six years together, he became engaged to Charles during a romantic birthday trip to Sri Lanka . The engagement was announced on Instagram with a post featuring an engagement ring emoji and the caption, "So this happened" . Charles confirmed the news in the comments section with a message that read, "6 years and counting…he said yes" . This public announcement provided fans and followers with a glimpse into his personal happiness and marked a significant personal event in his life. The couple's relationship appears to be a cornerstone of his personal life, and he has spoken about it openly, contributing to a public image that values authenticity and personal connection. The provided sources do not contain information regarding any previous relationships, marriages, or children, focusing exclusively on his current partnership with Charles. The emphasis on his marriage and his description of Charles as his "best friend" suggest a relationship built on a strong foundation of friendship and mutual respect, which he seems comfortable sharing with the public. This aspect of his life humanizes him and connects him with audiences on a more personal level, particularly within the context of contemporary discussions around LGBTQ+ relationships and family structures.

## Public Advocacy

Jimmy Essex has distinguished himself not only as a performer but also as a vocal advocate for his industry, using his platform to address public policy issues affecting the arts community in the United Kingdom. A prominent example of this advocacy occurred in an interview with PinkNews, where he publicly criticized the handling of the arts sector by the UK Conservative government during the COVID-19 pandemic . In the interview, he expressed significant frustration regarding what he described as the neglect of theatre and other live performance venues. He characterized the situation as relegating theatre to a "second-class job," articulating a perspective that resonates with many professionals in the field who faced prolonged closures and financial hardship during the pandemic . By making these statements, Essex positioned himself as a representative voice for artists and workers in the cultural sector, speaking out against policies he viewed as inadequate or dismissive of the value of live performance. His comments reflect a deep-seated belief in the importance of theatre, which he affirmed as his lifelong vocation . This public stance adds a layer of social and political engagement to his profile, portraying him as an artist who is invested in the health and future of the very industry he works within. His advocacy demonstrates a commitment to more than just his own career success; it shows a concern for the systemic challenges facing his peers and the broader cultural landscape of the UK.

His work has been covered by a range of publications, including entertainment-focused outlets and LGBTQ+-specific media like PinkNews, indicating a diverse readership and a public profile that intersects with both mainstream and niche interests , . His West End debut in *GHBoy* was highlighted as a significant career milestone, with particular attention paid to the personal resonance he felt for the role's exploration of gay identity and trauma . This suggests that his performance was viewed not just as a technical achievement but as a meaningful contribution to contemporary theatre discourse. Similarly, his portrayal of Adam Donovan in *Hollyoaks* was substantial enough to warrant a dramatic and memorable exit storyline, a testament to the impact of his performance on the show's narrative . His inclusion in high-profile projects like Netflix's *The Sandman* points to a perception of him as a credible and talented actor capable of meeting the demands of major productions . However, the sources do not mention any specific awards or nominations, nor do they detail any significant controversies or opposing viewpoints regarding his work. Therefore, his legacy remains that of a promising and versatile actor whose career is defined by a commitment to his craft, a willingness to engage with challenging material, and an active role in advocating for the arts. His ongoing work in theatre, television, and creative writing will likely continue to shape his reputation as a significant figure in British entertainment.

UK Theatre Newsletter Get all the top news & discounts for UK & beyond. ✨ Sign Up ![Image 36: Interview: Jimmy Essex Talks GHBOY at Charing Cross Theatre Image](https://cloudimages2.broadwayworld.com/columnpiccloud/21606063816.jpg?format=auto&width=1400) Jimmy Essex in _GHBoy_ Swapping the TV set of _Hollyoaks_ for the West End, Jimmy Essex is making his professional stage debut as Robert in _GHBoy_ at Charing Cross Theatre this month. ### LATEST NEWS [Jonas Kaufmann Says He Will Not Sing in Great Britain](https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Jonas-Kaufmann-Says-He-Will-Not-Sing-in-Great-Britain-20251222) [Photos: BEAUTIFUL LITTLE FOOL Artwork](https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Photos-David-Hunter-Lauren-Ward-and-Hannah-Corneau-in-BEAUTIFUL-LITTLE-FOOL-Artwork-20251222) [Final Weeks to Vote for the 2025 BroadwayWorld UK / West End Awards](https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Final-Weeks-to-Vote-for-the-2025-BroadwayWorld-UK-West-End-Awards-20251222) [Photos: In Rehearsal For ARCADIA at the Old Vic](https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Photos-In-Rehearsal-For-ARCADIA-at-the-Old-Vic-20251222) ### 🎭 NEW! UK Theatre Newsletter Get all the top news & discounts for UK & beyond. ✨ Sign Up We chatted to Jimmy about entering the theatre industry in a pandemic, the misconceptions of gay culture that the show addresses and why he loves playing challenging roles. **Can you explain the story of _GHBoy_, and the role of Robert, who you're playing?** The story is centred around Robert and his addiction to chemsex and cheating. It's about his discovery of himself, finding out who he is and coming to terms with something really terrible that happened to him and the major effect it's had on his life. **How are you feeling about making your West End debut?** Amazing, and it's been the most incredible experience so far. Coming into something so new and exciting in itself feels like such an achievement. It's something very different to anything I've ever done and I just love the challenge of it. I couldn't be happier really. **Does it feel odd to be making your debut during a pandemic?** Yeah, of course. But the good thing is, I have nothing to compare it to! I didn't know how it was going to work; to an extent, you're making the rules as you go along because nobody's faced this before, so we're just figuring things out as we go. There have been a few growing pains, but I think we're there now. We get how it has to work and how we can do it safely; it's been challenging, but also really exciting. **What drew you to go from your TV work to the theatre?** I love theatre, and theatre is what got me into acting anyway. I think as a medium, it's incredible; there's something so magical about it. I also wanted to push myself, and I love this role of Robert. I think the role really spoke to me; there's something about his journey of discovering himself that really scratched an itch for me, so I just jumped at the chance. ![Image 37: Interview: Jimmy Essex Talks GHBOY at Charing Cross Theatre Image](https://cloudimages2.broadwayworld.com/upload13/2076432/Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch-Marc-Bosch-Sergi-Castell_-Credit-Adam-Stevens-Productions-768x432.jpg?format=auto&width=1400) Jimmy Essex & Marc Bosch in _GHBoy_ **How are rehearsals going?** Great! They've been going really well. We're obviously having to do social distancing, we're getting tested quite regularly and we have to wear masks for some of it too. So it's all been learning how to adapt to this crazy new world we're living in. But it's been great - the cast is wonderful and the director, Jon Pashley is amazing. I know Paul Harvard, who wrote the play, from years and years ago, so it's been nice to reconnect with him as well. **It's Paul Harvard's debut play - is it nice to star in someone's debut work as your West End debut?** Yeah, definitely. I think because it's new and it's his first play, everyone wants to make it as amazing as it can be, just out of the love for it and because we want to make it special for everyone. Plus, we're the first people doing it, so there's something really exciting about that. We're paving the way for it, which is lovely. **The show tackles misconceptions around gay culture and promiscuity - why is this such an important message?** I think there are taboos and a hushness around a lot of gay culture; not just from the heterosexual community to the gay community, but also within the gay community too. There are a lot of misconceptions and stigma that come with certain lifestyles and choices. So, I think it's really good to put a human face on this subject and make it relatable. I just think it's really important to shine a light on it. **The show has a very diverse cast with a range of ages and experiences, both on stage and behind the scenes. That must be a great team to be part of.** Yeah, definitely. I think we all feel very blessed. Not only because we're trying to do something that seems impossible, but also because of the range of people involved and the experiences they're bringing to the project. I think it says so much about what we want the message to be; it's about acceptance of everyone. ![Image 38: Interview: Jimmy Essex Talks GHBOY at Charing Cross Theatre Image](https://cloudimages2.broadwayworld.com/upload13/2076432/Sylvester-Akinrolabu-Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch_-Credit-Adam-Stevens-Productions.jpg?format=auto&width=1400) Jimmy Essex and Sylvester Akinrolabu in _GHBoy_ **It's been a really weird year. How have you been coping during the pandemic?** To be honest, at first, I loved it. Once I focused on just getting back to basics, appreciating what I have and the people I have around me, as well as the magic and the enjoyment in everyday life, there was something really special about that. I loved it. Then about halfway through, I was pulling my hair out. I'm quite an active person and I love to be doing things, and so it's been quite a struggle. I think the one good thing I took from it was the fact I was with my partner the whole time and we got to actually spend some time together, which is a rarity. And also, just finding enjoyment; my garden has never looked so good! **You're about to make your debut, but what would your dream theatre role be in the future?** Any kind of theatre that inspires some kind of conversation, and a role that is as challenging as Robert in _GHBoy_. I think those are the things that I look forward to, and as I'm growing in my career, are things that make me question myself and normatives that I may have already created in my own brain. Those juicy roles where it changes not only the audience, but my perspective of things, that's what appeals to me the most. **Why should people come and see _GHBoy_?** We're putting on this amazing show, so come and support theatre! I think it will surprise people too. I think people have a misconception about what the play is going to be about and how they're going to feel about it. I think they'll walk out with a completely new mindset, having gone on this amazing journey with this guy. I think there's something really, really special about that. _GHBoy at Charing Cross Theatre [from 3 December](http://ticketsareavailablenow/)_ _Photo credit: Adam Stevens_ ### NEXT UP [FOR **Beyond** offers an experience **like no other** with industry **professional teachers** delivering **first hand insight** into the **world of performing arts**…

Beyond Performing Arts
----------------------

**Beyond Performing Arts** is an **innovative** and **exciting** new **performing arts schoo**l founded by **Jimmy Essex** and **Francesca Lyons** in 2018.

**Beyond** offers an experience like no other with **industry professional teachers** delivering first hand insight into the **world of performing arts**.

Teachers credits include **Hollyoaks, X-Factor, Britain’s got Talent**, and various **international cruise ships** to name a few! As well as regular classes, **Beyond** offers **West End/TV acting** **workshops** throughout the year led by cast members of the West end’s leading shows and some of the biggest names in television.

Since opening, the school has seen a great amount of success and word of mouth spread fast about the fun, high energy and **current** classes Beyond has to offer.

Classes start from ages 4 and above in acting, singing and dancing and all levels are welcome.

If you haven’t already heard enough, **Francesca** and **Jimmy** invite you for a **free trial day** where you can come and experience all **Beyond** has to offer for yourself.

Meet Our amazing  
Dance Teachers
---------------------------------

#### Francesca **Lyons**

**Singing, Dance and Musical Theatre Teacher**

Francesca found her passion for singing and performing at a young age and met Jimmy at 14 where they trained at a theatre school together until they auditioned for professional college. Francesca trained for 3 years at the prestigious Urdang Academy where she trained extensively in acting, dancing and singing. After leaving, Francesca worked nonstop as a vocalist and went from contract to contract on various cruise ships as vocalist and a dancer.

Francesca has sung a very vast range of styles and studied vocally how to approach different ways of singing. Francesca has worked in the recording studio too and is a front singer for the cover band Penthouse 5.

Francesca trained over the years in The Estill model and studied anatomy of the voice and how to break down and teach various vocal styles. Francesca studied how to work with adolescent voices and it is her pleasure to coach and teach children how to sing safely yet gain confidence to explore and push their voices (safely) beyond their inhibitions and insecurities.

#### Jimmy **Essex**

**Acting & Dance Teacher / Choreographer**

Jimmy has already had a long and rich career in all areas of the performing arts industry. After completing training at The Urdang Academy in London, he jumped straight into professional dancing, appearing in shows like The X factor and Britain’s Got Talent.

He has toured with major UK artists including The Saturdays and even performed at Capital FM’s winter and summer time balls. More recently, Jimmy appeared in the hit channel 4 show Hollyoaks where he played Adam Donovan for 2 years. He was also the face of the Euro cup Coca Cola advert. Bringing all of his experiences to teaching, Jimmy adds true insight into the professional world of performing arts.

Jimmy has a true passion for creating a safe and fun environment for kids to learn and grow in the industry he loves so much.

Can life truly imitate art?

For one unforgettable night, on Wednesday, November 15th 2023 at Marylebone Theatre, Ye You Productions is set to bring a series of riveting performances from the canvas to the stage.

Picture This promises to take audiences on an exciting journey of ekphrastic storytelling, showcasing a diverse range of new writing by established and emerging literary talents nestled amongst a curated collection of timeless classics.

George Chilcott (String v SPITTA, Songlines, Swansong) will be directing the evening, consolidating the writing into a mesmerising theatrical experience, united by the shared theme and challenge of writing in response to art. Our audience will become immersed in the artwork whilst witnessing its transformation into a live performance.

The impressive literary line-up includes award-winning writers Mike Bartlett (Cock, Dr Foster, Bull) and Amy Rosenthal (Sitting Pretty, Henna Night), as well as the brilliant minds of Barney Fishwick, Philippa Lawford, John Akinde, Oliver Forsyth, Joe McArdle, Georgia Frost, Samson Ajewole, Sophie Bentinck, Jimmy Essex and hand picked work from David Ireland all of our writers have thoughtfully penned pieces for the night alone, so Picture This will be your only opportunity to see them performed.

Externalising inspiration has proved an exciting challenge for our writers - “With this project the process had to change. Instead of waiting for a character to emerge, new and fully formed, I had to piece one together from the work in front of me. This changed it from a solo exercise into a conversation with someone I'd never met” - Oliver Forsyth

Don't miss your chance to be part of this unique celebration of the blurred lines between art forms and the many ways creativity begets more of itself.

Reserve your tickets [here](https://www.marylebonetheatre.com/productions/picture-this) for PICTURE THIS and be part of an unforgettable evening.

**ALL PROCEEDS**  
At Ye You Productions, we believe in supporting the next generation of artists. That's why we're thrilled to announce that all proceeds from ticket sales will be dedicated to a private charitable trust committed to providing financial aid and resources to emerging artists. By eliminating financial barriers, the trust supports artists to focus on and further their practice.

**OUR DIRECTOR**  
George Chilcott founded DugOut Theatre in 2012 and continues to be the company’s Artistic Director. George also directs comedy and is the director of Edinburgh Comedy Award Nominated sketch duo Goodbear.  
Some credits include; String v SPITTA (Soho Theatre), Agatha (Theatre 503), Goodbear: Dougal (Soho Theatre), Songlines (HighTide Theatre), Replay (Theatre E59E/ Brits Off Broadway), Swansong (Lowry Theatre) and Inheritance Blues (Soho Theatre). In 2022, George loves to make work that is big-hearted, funny, musical and, above all, tells a good story.

**OUR WRITERS**  
Mike Bartlett is an English playwright and screenwriter for film and TV series. His 2015 psychological thriller TV series, Doctor Foster, starring Suranne Jones, won the New Drama award from National Television Awards. Bartlett's play Bull won Best New Play at The National Theatre Awards. Cock starring Andrew Scott and Ben Whishaw won Laurence Olivier Award for Outstanding Achievement in an Affiliate Theatre alongside King Charles III which won Olivier Award for Best New Play.

Amy Rosenthal is an acclaimed playwright whose work has been performed internationally. Stage plays include Sitting Pretty, Henna Night and On The Rocks (nominated for the Susan Smith Blackburn Prize). Amy currently has a screenplay in development with Atlas Films. Her most recent play, The Party Girls will be produced by the Marlowe Theatre, Canterbury, and she is under commission to Manhattan Theatre Club.

Georgia Frost is an Actor, Writer and Maker. Although writing has always been a part of Georgia’s practice, sharing their work is fairly new. Currently in the works is a short film and one man show Georgia hopes to stage in the new year. Acting credits include: Henry V (The Globe), Gaia (BBC Short Film), This Is Going To Hurt (BBC), Dead Dog In A Suitcase (Kneehigh), The Other One (BBC) and Monster Calls (Old Vic).

Oliver Forsyth is a writer for theatre and television. He currently has two plays under commission and is developing original TV scripts. Previous work includes 'Cash Cow' (Hampstead Theatre) 'Kings' (New Diorama Theatre) and 'Such Filthy F\*cks' (The Pleasance/New Diorama Theatre/Smoke & Oakum Theatre)'.

Philippa Lawford is a writer-director from London. Her debut play, Ikaria, won a runner-up award from the ATG Playwrights’ Prize and an OFFIE Short Run Commendation, and was named no. 2 on Broadway World’s list of Best Theatre of 2022. Ikaria returns to London after a 7 venue UK tour in Autumn, this time to the Park Theatre.

Samson Ajewole is an actor and emerging writer. Having most recently written BFI-funded short film ‘ An Eighth of Him’ He is best known for being featured in HBO’s Bafta award-winning series 'I May Destroy You' and most recently appearing in “ A Little Life” at the Savoy Theatre.

West End chemsex drama star Jimmy Essex is determined to tell queer stories beyond ‘the coming out thing’
=========================================================================================================

*   Dec 11 2020
*   Written by [Josh Milton](https://www.thepinknews.com/author/josh-milton/)

*   Share
    
    [](https://twitter.com/share?text=https://www.thepinknews.com/2020/12/11/jimmy-essex-ghboy-charing-cross-theatre-london-coronavirus-boris-johnson/)[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.thepinknews.com/2020/12/11/jimmy-essex-ghboy-charing-cross-theatre-london-coronavirus-boris-johnson/)[](https://reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thepinknews.com%2F2020%2F12%2F11%2Fjimmy-essex-ghboy-charing-cross-theatre-london-coronavirus-boris-johnson%2F)[](https://www.thepinknews.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#)[](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thepinknews.com%2F2020%2F12%2F11%2Fjimmy-essex-ghboy-charing-cross-theatre-london-coronavirus-boris-johnson%2F)[](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thepinknews.com%2F2020%2F12%2F11%2Fjimmy-essex-ghboy-charing-cross-theatre-london-coronavirus-boris-johnson%2F)
    
*   Save for later
*   Comment
    

![Image 3: Jimmy Essex's face against a dimly lit wall](https://www.thepinknews.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/jimmy_essex-3-2.jpg?w=792&h=416&crop=1)

Jimmy Essex is set to make his theatre debut in GHBoy. (Supplied)

Jimmy Essex is set to make his theatre debut in GHBoy. (Supplied)

Jimmy Essex had two things on his mind as he swerved out of the way of a car as he crossed the road: deciding what sandwich to grab from Pret a Manger and just how furious he is with Boris Johnson.

The British prime minister, and the bungled way his government had handled the coronavirus’ impact on the country’s once-thriving and beloved arts sector, is on the actor’s mind. A lot.

“Every day feels like a gift at the moment because we just don’t know what’s going on,” Essex told _PinkNews_, “especially with what’s been going on with the arts.

“I think it’s been quite neglected, it’s really been pushed aside and treated as a second-class job.”

“I think nobody’s gonna get it right,” he said of the Conservative Party’s coronavirus approach, noting he “feels bad” for Johnson. Nevertheless: “I would rather the rules be really, really strict and make f\*\*king sense. It’s quite frustrating.

“But I don’t think I’m qualified to tell him anything. I can slag \[Johnson\] off on the sidelines, but I’m not sure I could do anything better.”

Essex, 36, had taken his lunch break from rehearsals for _[GHBoy](https://charingcrosstheatre.co.uk/theatre/ghboy)_ at the Charing Cross Theatre when he spoke with _PinkNews_.

The production, which opened on 3 December and written by Paul Harvard, dives deep into the darker underbelly of chemsex – a sub-culture of queer men that use drugs such as GHB to facilitate sex acts.

Experts have sought to [reclassify the date rape drug from Class C to a Class B drug](https://thepinknews.com/2020/11/20/ghb-chemsex-reynhard-sinaga-stephen-port-rape-advisory-council-drug-class-b/) – underscoring the severity of its side-effects when overdosed and how it has been weaponised by killers.

Essex will play Robert Finch, a gay man more or less counting down his own self-destruct sequence. Grieving the death of his father, he smokes, drinks and shoulders the anguish of an East London queer community cowed into fear by a killer targeting young men.

It’s a lot. And in the throes of his inner-turmoil, Robert’s boyfriend proposes – a question that prompts him to interrogate why he so often resorts to self-sabotage.

“What drew me to it was his innocence and his vulnerability,” Essex said, known for his former role as Adam Donovan in _Hollyoaks_. “I think he’s like a child. He doesn’t know what he’s doing a lot of the time.

![Image 4](https://thepinknews.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch-Marc-Bosch-Sergi-Castell.-Credit-Bettina-John-1024x744.jpg)Jimmy Essex (L) and Mark Bosch. (Bettinia John)

“And I think there’s so much to be said about that. There are selfish people. And there are people that do so without realising it – I think he’s one of the good guys.”

**Jimmy Essex: ‘Theatre will come back fighting’**
--------------------------------------------------

Essex had an almost bubbly tone to his voice as he described _GHBoy_, propping it up as if he were protective of it. But he has every reason to – it’s both his stage debut and a way to wrestle with his own inner demons, he said.

“I think I can get wrapped up in myself, ” he mused, “which I think we all have, and I’ve made choices based on things that I’ve wanted, and not maybe looked at who that may be hurting.

“\[Like Robert\] I’ve made those discoveries, and I’ve done that journey myself, playing it through someone else’s just another way of, of working through your own stuff.”

The “challenge” of theatre, he said, felt like a “blessing” to get involved with after months of hunkering down during lockdown with his [husband and “best friend”, Charles](https://thepinknews.com/2019/01/22/hollyoaks-jimmy-essex-engaged-charles/).

In an effort to squash the stale, almost fetid stress of being stuck at home, his room quickly became a tossed salad of scripts and ideas for short films. Essex said he is determined to help tell LGBT+ stories beyond the “coming out thing” that has long bound queer storytellers.

“That tends to be a lot of what’s on telly, and I kinda was like, what after that? What’s there?”

![Image 5](https://thepinknews.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Jimmy-Essex-Robert-Finch.-Credit-Bettina-John-1024x749.jpg)_GHBoy_ follows Robert Finch (Jimmy Essex) as he battles his fear that he will never love again. (Bettinia John)

But in capturing the resilience and wit of British theatre, Essex said that even as the coronavirus chucks the industry into jeopardy, putting GHBoy on amid it all “really feels like a ‘f\*\*k you’.”

“I do think it’s a shame that theatre hasn’t been something that \[the government\] are fighting for when I do know that other countries have really put a lot into it.

“When when it has such a huge impact in this country. They do come to the country to see theatre and we’re like one of the epicentres of it.

“So I find it quite disheartening that it’s always a bit like, oh, we’ll just suck it up and find another job. It doesn’t really work like that.

“It’s my life. And this is what I have been trying to do my whole life,”  he said, stressing that he’s not retraining in cyber anytime soon.

“But I do think in times that these things come back fighting, people are going to be desperate to go out people like they were to restaurants. We’re playing it will be the same effect.

“So hopefully, hopefully, everybody comes out fine.”

_GHBoy will run at the Charing Cross Theatre from 3-20 December 2020. Tickets are available [here](https://charingcrosstheatre.co.uk/theatre/ghboy)._
